newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Archer met on budget - Washington Post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Archer met on budget - Washington Post.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, and President Bill Clinton met for over an hour on Friday to discuss tax policy, Medicare, Social Security and other budget matters, the Washington Post reported in Sunday editions.
Archer suggested the meeting to discuss upcoming legislative issues, but a top administration official said the meeting was a "courtesy call" and "not a budget negotiation," the paper reported.
In a telephone interview with the paper, Archer declined to elaborate on the meeting, saying the two men agreed to keep the details private.

"We both expressed a desire to find areas of common ground. There was a discussion of these issues, but no attempt to get into specifics and no attempt to reach any final conclusion," Archer told the Post.

Archer stressed his willingness to be flexible in resolving tax policy issues with the administration. He said Republicans and the White House are in general agreement on a host of tax issues, the Post reported.

He said both sides favored a $500-per-child tax credit for middle-income families; expanded incentives for participation in tax-favored individual retirement accounts; and additional capital gains tax relief for homeowners.
The Texas Republican also signaled support for Clinton campaign proposals to offer new tax breaks for students, despite misgivings about how such proposals would be implemented.
Archer also told the newspaper that Clinton's proposals for blunting the impact of welfare reform would get a fair hearing in his committee.
But Archer said congressional Republicans would be unwilling to approve overall tax relief without "some kind of reduction in the capital gains tax."
Clinton will submit a budget proposal for 1998 to Congress in February.
